summary.text: James Wiley, a Republican political consultant and former executive director of the Libertarian Party of Colorado, lost the November 3, 2026 election for secretary of state of Colorado to Amanda Gonzalez.
He ran as a Libertarian for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District in 2024 before switching parties.
His campaign called for decertifying electronic voting machines and moving to hand-counted paper ballots.

paragraphs.text: Wiley was born in Colorado Springs and describes himself as a fifth-generation Colorado native.
He says he spent part of his youth in Kazakhstan, where he saw the fall of communism, before moving back to the family homestead at 15 and graduating from Pueblo County High School.
He earned a management and marketing degree and a master's degree in business administration at Colorado State University Pueblo, the latter in 2017.
Wiley works as a political consultant.
He has been executive director of the Libertarian Party of Colorado, director of Project Thaler and Save Our Suffrage, and secretary of the Chainsaw Caucus.
He says he has filed or supported lawsuits over election systems, including against Dominion Voting Systems and Secretary of State Jena Griswold.
Wiley was the Libertarian candidate for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District in 2024, finishing third with 2.7 percent of the vote behind Republican Jeff Hurd and Democrat Adam Frisch.
He then switched to the Republican Party and advanced unopposed from the June 30, 2026, Republican primary for Secretary of State.

His platform called for decertifying electronic voting equipment, one-day in-person voting with voter ID and hand-counted paper ballots, and placing public records on a blockchain ledger; he also said he would release internal Secretary of State files related to the case of Tina Peters.
He received 36.8% of the vote to Amanda Gonzalez's 60.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
